title: GEMM scheduling
brief: Count waves, partition K for split-K and stream-K, order tiles for a persistent kernel, fuse an epilogue, and choose a schedule from a cost model. Then write Triton split-K, persistent, and fused-epilogue kernels and compare them with torch.matmul on tall-skinny shapes.
hints: Start with wave_stats. It needs no other function. Round each dimension up to whole tiles first: ceil(m / tile_m) * ceil(n / tile_n). Waves are tiles divided by ctas_per_sm * sm_count, rounded up.

split_k_ranges deals k_iters like cards: base = k_iters // splits, and the first k_iters % splits ranges take one more. The last K-iteration of split_k_matmul can be shorter than block_k, so clip the column range to K.
split_k_matmul converts each slice to float32 before the matmul and keeps every partial in float32. Rounding a partial to the input dtype loses about 2^-11 of its value.
reduce_partials must add one float32 at a time. Python floats are float64, which hides the order dependence: use torch.tensor(x, dtype=torch.float32) for the accumulator.
stream_k_plan: CTA c starts at c * base + min(c, rem) in the global iteration order. Cut its range at every multiple of iters_per_tile to get segments with tile-local k.
persistent_tile_order uses the same grouped arithmetic as lab 14, applied to the tile ids cta, cta + ctas, and so on. group_size_m is min(tiles_m - first_pid_m, group_m).
epilogue_bytes counts C-sized traffic only. A fused epilogue writes C once. An unfused one writes C, then every stage reads m * n elements and writes m * n elements.
schedule_cost_us is max(compute, memory) plus extra. Scale the memory time by sm_count / active, where active is the number of CTAs that run at once, capped at sm_count.
The Triton kernels run only on a GPU. A work item of the persistent kernel is one (tile, split) pair, and splits above 1 add partials with tl.atomic_add into a zeroed float32 buffer.
Compiling the first Triton kernel takes several seconds, and the tests call each kernel for many shapes, so allow a few minutes of run time.
